title: How many lotuses are there after both ponds?
description: A lotus grows for four days in a doubling pond and four days in a tripling pond, and pairing each two with a three gives one power. The same idea finds two to the power five times five to the power five. Keeko's doubt is that two plus three gives five to the power four.
teaching_notes: One idea: powers with the same exponent are joined by pairing the bases, so the bases are multiplied and the exponent stays. Watch for students who add the bases instead of multiplying them.

source: Damayanti puts a lotus in the doubling pond for 4 days and t
video_script.why: The child can join powers of one number and now meets two ponds, one doubling and one tripling, and joins powers that have different bases but the same exponent.
video_script.substitution: The book's own two ponds with four days in each, and the book's own two to the power five times five to the power five.
video_script.anchor: two ponds on the board, one doubling and one tripling, with the lotuses moving from the first pond to the second
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the answer is five to the power four, because two plus three is five. Each two is paired with one three by multiplying, so each pair is six, and five to the power four is only six hundred twenty five.
video_script.payoff_line: There are one thousand two hundred ninety six lotuses either way

final_answer.value: 1296 lotuses either way; 2 to the power 5 × 5 to the power 5 is 100000
final_answer.spoken: one thousand two hundred ninety six lotuses either way; two to the power five times five to the power five is one lakh

names.{{NAME_3}}: moves the lotuses from the doubling pond to the tripling pond

video_script.design: One idea: pair each base and keep the exponent. The two ponds stay on the board all video; the two values are left open until the answer; one slip at the end.

beats.on_screen: title card, From your book; two ponds, one marked doubles every day and one marked triples every day

marks.book: the title card From your book arrives
marks.ponds: the two ponds appear side by side
marks.moves: one lotus appears in the doubling pond and an arrow runs to the tripling pond
marks.ask: a question mark appears over the tripling pond

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about two lotus ponds.
<bookmark mark='ponds'/>One pond doubles its lotuses every day, and the other triples them.
<bookmark mark='moves'/>{{NAME_3}} puts one lotus in the doubling pond for four days.
Then all the lotuses move to the tripling pond for four days.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many lotuses are there at the end?
And can the same idea find two to the power five times five to the power five?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: doubling: × 2 each day; tripling: × 3 each day; 4 days of doubling: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2

marks.double: × 2 and × 3 arrows appear over the two ponds
marks.days: four 2s are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='double'/>Doubling multiplies by two each day, and tripling multiplies by three each day.
<bookmark mark='days'/>Four days of doubling means four twos multiplied.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 lotus; 4 days doubling, then 4 days tripling; 2⁵ × 5⁵

marks.given: 1 lotus and 4 days of doubling are written
marks.then: then 4 days of tripling is written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, {{NAME_3}} starts with one lotus in the doubling pond for four days.
<bookmark mark='then'/>Then all the lotuses go to the tripling pond for four days.
<bookmark mark='also'/>We also have two to the power five times five to the power five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the lotuses at the end; the value of 2⁵ × 5⁵
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number of lotuses at the end.
<bookmark mark='value'/>Then we work out the value of the second power.

marks.one: four 2s are written in a row after 1

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, four days of doubling make four twos multiplied.
<bookmark mark='sixteen'/>That is two to the power four, which is sixteen lotuses.

marks.open: 16 × 81 is written with the result left open

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, four days of tripling multiply by four threes.
<bookmark mark='power'/>That is two to the power four times three to the power four.
<bookmark mark='open'/>Sixteen times eighty one is left to find.

beats.on_screen: 2⁴ × 3⁴ = (2 × 3) × (2 × 3) × (2 × 3) × (2 × 3) = (2 × 3)⁴ = 6⁴; swapping the ponds gives 3⁴ × 2⁴, the same four pairs

marks.three: each 2 is paired with one 3 in four pairs
marks.swap: 3⁴ × 2⁴ is written with the same four pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, pair each two with one three.
<bookmark mark='six'/>That is two times three, four times, which is six to the power four.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>Swapping the ponds gives the same four pairs.

marks.four: each 2 is paired with one 5 in five pairs
marks.open: the value of 10⁵ is left open

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, pair each two with one five in the second power.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>That is two times five, five times, which is ten to the power five.
<bookmark mark='open'/>The value of ten to the power five is left to find.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>There are one thousand two hundred ninety six lotuses either way.
Sixteen times eighty one is one thousand two hundred ninety six.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Six to the power four gives the same number.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Two to the power five times five to the power five is ten to the power five.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>That is thirty two times three thousand one hundred twenty five, which is one lakh.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two ponds
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 2 + 3 = 5 and 5⁴ appear, then are crossed out; the pairs are shown as 2 × 3 = 6; 5⁴ = 625 is shown smaller than the lotuses counted

marks.pairs: 5⁴ is crossed out and each pair is marked 2 × 3 = 6
marks.count: 5⁴ = 625 is shown as a short bar beside the long bar of lotuses counted

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is five to the power four, because two plus three is five.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>But each two is paired with one three by multiplying, so each pair is six, not five.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Five to the power four is only six hundred twenty five, far fewer than the lotuses we counted.
